History:
- Chief complaint: 26-year-old woman with a headache for about 3 days, primarily around the right eye but involving the whole head; described as dull most of the time with episodic sharpness; pain rated ~8/10.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began at work ~3 days ago, gradually worsened, present most of the time with fluctuating intensity; waking with worse pain.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia (light worsens pain); nausea/sick feeling but no vomiting; neck stiffness reported; difficulty focusing at work; no reported fever or rashes; no focal weakness or speech difficulties; no vision loss.
- Triggers/relief: Tried ibuprofen with minimal relief over the last 2 days; possible dehydration or stress considered; high screen time at work; wearing glasses; no regular medications.
- Past medical history: History of headaches; no personal history of migraines reported. Family history positive for migraines (mother and sister). Eye history: wears glasses since age 5; no recent eye test noted.
- Medications/allergies/social factors: No regular medications; allergies to medications not known. Socially smokes and drinks; lives with three housemates; IT work with high screen time and stress.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Not recorded
- Allergies: No known drug allergies
- Prior hospitalizations: Not recorded
- Medications: Ibuprofen used self-medically for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented); no other regular meds

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded (no vital signs or formal exam documented in transcript)

Impression:
- Probable migraine headache (migraine without aura) given unilateral/right-hemispheric involvement, photophobia, nausea, gradual onset over several days, and family history of migraines.
- Differential considerations (consistent with transcript): Tension-type headache; meningitis/encephalitis (less likely due to lack of fever/altered mental status); medication-overuse headache (MOH) considered given recent NSAID use.

Management Plan:
- Acute pharmacologic options discussed:
  - Optimize NSAID dosing: increase ibuprofen dosing to up to two tablets, three times daily.
  - Consider alternative analgesics: naproxen option; paracetamol; codeine if needed.
- Nonpharmacologic/monitoring:
  - Headache diary to identify triggers and pattern.
  - Schedule follow-up in about 1–2 weeks; return sooner if symptoms worsen or if new neurological symptoms develop (vision changes, weakness, confusion).
  - If headaches continue or worsen with possible migraine pattern, discuss prophylactic therapy at follow-up.
- Counseling:
  - If visual symptoms or neurological deficits emerge, seek urgent care.

Patient Summary:
- Adriana presents with a 3-day, predominantly right-eyed headache with photophobia and nausea, not relieved by over-the-counter ibuprofen. The clinician suspects a migraine and plans to escalate treatment (consider naproxen or other analgesics), start a headache diary, and arrange a follow-up in 1–2 weeks, with instructions to return if symptoms worsen or new neuro-visual signs appear.

Key Takeaways:
- Consider a migraine as the leading diagnosis; use a stepped analgesic plan (increase NSAID dosing or add acetaminophen/codeine as appropriate).
- Maintain a headache diary to identify triggers; follow up in 1–2 weeks.
- Seek urgent care if vision changes, new weakness, fever, or altered mental status occur.

Next Steps:
- Prescribe appropriate stronger analgesia today (naproxen or paracetamol ± codeine as discussed) and provide ibuprofen dosing guidance (up to two tablets three times daily if chosen).
- Provide patient with headache diary instructions; arrange follow-up in 7–14 days; advise return sooner if red flags or deterioration.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing elements: Vital signs and a formal physical examination are not documented; no imaging or laboratory results discussed.
- Potential conflicts: None between transcript and differential diagnosis (no contradictory statements).
- Transcript quality: Some portions of the patient interview are informal; key clinical details (neuro exam, vitals) were not captured in the note due to missing documentation.
